name: 3S Viking Status (GMCP)
author: Joakim
description: The settlement half of the Viking HUD, fed by the Guild.* GMCP packages (3Scapes only; the MIP-fed original ships as '3S Viking Status (classic, MIP)' - run one or the other, they answer to the same commands). Tabs: Stats / City / Builds / Production / People / Settlers / Holds / Trade / Trade Auto / Trade Log / Feeds - everywhere you travel TO lives in 3s-viking-world, and the travel engine, vgo/vhere and the mission runner went with it - this is the settlement half now. The city plan is still computed here (Guild.City feeds it, `vplan` edits it); only its picture is drawn there. Includes the build planner and the market scanner + auto-trader. Warehouse stock comes straight from the Guild.Warehouse feed (server-side since 28 Aug) with real per-grade freshness; the `vtrade stock` text scan - Refresh button, `vstock`, cart-event and staleness re-scans - remains only as the automatic fallback for a server without that package. An incoming raid (Guild.City raid) shows on the Stats tab's War section, damaged buildings (bdmg) on the Builds tab, and the four guild-xp tracks (buandi/drotta/viga/vitka off Guild.State.gxp - current, advance threshold, last gain) in the Stats tab's GXP section. Per-good stock floors ('atrade floor grain 500') keep a minimum of a good in the warehouse whatever the category reserve says - floored names show blue in the Trade tab, held (never-traded) names amber; the Trade tab's Floor box sets the value, and a right-click on a good's name opens a menu (host API 1.19) - hold/release, set the floor, clear it - with plain rclick=/click= fallbacks for older hosts. The auto-trader knows the cartyard's one-caravan-per-3-minutes rhythm: it holds after every dispatch, reads the yard's own 'Ready in' refusal to set the clock exactly, and never spams doomed carts into the cooldown ('atrade yard <sec>' tunes the hold). Market prices come straight from the Guild.TradeGoods feed (per-village, pushed; the 30 good codes solved mechanically and cross-validated), so the mkref scan burst is retired to a fallback. The trader treats a town's demand as an answer: zero demand gets no cart however good the price, and every dispatched cart provisionally debits the town's demand (or supply, for buys) locally, so quiet stretches between feed pushes can't stack a second caravan into demand the first already claimed - the next feed row restores the server's truth. Remaining GMCP feed gaps show honestly in their tabs.
